name: Abbie's World in-game HUD rubric
source_enum_note: source values are the identity schema's enum (docs/oracle/identity/game-identity.schema.json): footage_cv = computer vision over our own captures, llm_judge = VLM with saved prompt, pairwise and both orders, playtrace = in-game timing log, human = Evan or a child playtest, estimate = not yet measured.

examples: Sons of the Forest backpack mat
This War of Mine noise rings
Sons of the Forest grey screen

tiers.T0_world: state the world shows by itself; no UI
tiers.T1_on_thing: spatial or diegetic, attached to one thing
tiers.T2_always_on: overlay, at most 3 elements: tools and time
tiers.T3_summoned: detail on one gesture (hold, pinch, tap)
tiers.T4_workbench: grown-up controls behind a door (GAME_FEEL Law 12)

loss.sound: soft low note, never a buzzer

juice.reduced_motion: 150 ms crossfades, counters tick in place, no pulses; sound stays
juice.note: These are our design targets, not measurements of the studied games.

gates.check: Union area of always-on overlay elements <= 8% of the viewport, in portrait and landscape.
gates.method: manifest bboxes; or footage_cv: mask of non-world pixels over a capture

gates.check: Zero words visible in play mode. Numbers, the child's own names and the app's own name on the home screen are exempt.
gates.method: manifest word counts; OCR over captures

gates.check: Every touchable element >= 64 px (grown-up doors >= 44 px) and fully inside the safe area and outside the 20 px left back-swipe strip.
No information reachable only by hover; every hover preview has a touch twin (hold or drag).
gates.method: manifest flags; playtrace with a touch-only input device

gates.check: Every numeral cap height >= 18 px and contrast >= 3:1 against the worst background behind it across day, dusk and night captures.
gates.method: manifest + captures: luminance of glyph colour vs 5th and 95th percentile of a ring around the bbox

gates.check: No other game's UI art, icon, badge, font or layout copied; provenance lists every image source; no source-game screenshot used as a reference image.
No red alarm states, no buzzer sounds, no flashing above 3 Hz, no fail or game-over screens, meta effects never frightening.
gates.method: manifest flags; llm judge over a 30 s capture

checks.check: From a 1 s exposure of a capture, a VLM (and later a child) answers: time of day, is a card in hand, which animal wants something. Score = correct / 3, averaged over 5 captures.
Always-on elements keep the same anchor across all captures (centre drift <= 2% of the short edge).
At most 3 always-on elements.
Every element declares exactly one tier T0 to T4; T2 items justify themselves as needed every few seconds and changing the next action.
Every T3 item is reachable in one gesture from play.
At least 70% of state readouts (elements with readout=true) are spatial, diegetic, meta or none.
Every always-on meter has a world or meta echo (e.g. the sun dial and the light).
Numerals and icons over the world have an outline >= 8% of glyph height or a solid token behind them.
A VLM names every icon from a black silhouette at 32 px.
Every colour-coded element has a shape or icon twin; passes deuteranopia and protanopia simulation.
Always-on icons >= 48 px; spatial bubbles 36 to 56 px across the zoom range.
Elements touched more than once a minute sit in the bottom 40% of the screen in portrait.
Held items and placement previews render >= 60 px above the touch point.
One finger pans, two pinch and twist, hold summons; no modifier keys, no double-tap zoom.
Both orientations pass G1 and G3 with the same anchors.
Manifest declares focus, change, idle and threshold fade rules and a summon-all gesture.
Playtrace timings within 20% of the declared values.
The same element fades the same way in 10 of 10 repeats.
Every gain starts at its world source and flies to its counter.
Losses show a trailing ghost for >= 300 ms.
Thresholds pulse and start a world echo.
Every HUD change has a sound with pitch variation.
prefers-reduced-motion path present.
Pairwise judge vs a web-panel control: 'which looks like objects from this toy world?' wins both orders.
Play-mode CSS has no 1px solid borders on rectangles, no system-ui font stacks for visible text, no web icon sets, no hover-only colour changes.
Play-mode code has no panel/sidebar/toolbar/drawer/modal/toast/tabs/dropdown/select/input without a recorded reason (GAME_FEEL section 8).
Every sound cue has a visual twin (mute test still readable).
Colour-blind simulation keeps every cue distinct.
Pairwise judge: closer to Abbie's World references (Ranch tiles, cards, toy table) than to any single studied game's HUD.
